aggressive_definition: Advanced prostate cancer defined as stages C, D, or fatal cases.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: We examined the relationship of fat consumption to the incidence of advanced prostate cancer (stages C, D, or fatal cases) and to the total incidence of prostate cancer.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: As of January 31, 1990, 300 new cases of prostate cancer, including 126 advanced cases, were documented in 47855 participants initially free of diagnosed cancer.
reason: The abstract explicitly analyzes both total incident prostate cancer and incident advanced prostate cancer among participants initially free of diagnosed cancer. Advanced disease comprises stages C, D, or fatal cases.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Red meat represented the food group with the strongest positive association with advanced cancer (RR = 2.64; 95% CI = 1.21-5.77; P = .02).
estimate_classifications.reason: The red-meat estimate explicitly concerns incident advanced prostate cancer.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Saturated fat, monounsaturated fat, and alpha-linolenic acid, but not linoleic acid, were associated with advanced prostate cancer risk; only the association with alpha-linolenic acid persisted when saturated fat, monounsaturated fat, linoleic acid, and alpha-linolenic acid were modeled simultaneously (multivariate RR = 3.43; 95% CI = 1.67-7.04; P [trend] = .002).
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied effect is for advanced prostate cancer, but the reported exposure is specifically alpha-linolenic acid rather than total omega-3 fatty acids or total polyunsaturated fat.
